column1: # Documented "different engine" exceptions (PHASE4.md): one per line, numbers from the oracle (SF19 Lite vs SF16 d22) and the chess.com rule that explains the difference.

column4: different top move: 9...Bxg4 and 9...Nxg4 both take the blundered queen; SF16 d22 Bxg4 -578 vs Nxg4 -574 (4 cp), SF19 d22 Nxg4 -758 first, Lite mpv5 rank 2 (dump Bxg4 -7.63 vs Nxg4 -7.23); chess.com labels Bxg4 Excellent = not its top move, and Great needs the top move. Punish-a-blunder Great (rating 243) is right for whichever capture is the engine top.

different engine at the B-E3 boundary: 25.Rd5 (rook en prise, sacrifice 5) is not the top move; SF19 Lite d1d4 +1.08 vs Rd5 +0.74 = loss 0.0313 > 0.03 at 1660, SF16 d22 d1d4 +107 vs Rd5 +77 (rank 2) = loss 0.027 < 0.03, so on chess.com's engine numbers our rules give Brilliant.

chess.com's own engine disagrees with its label: SF16 d22 ranks 12.Bxb5 outside its top 5 (f1h3 +380 ... Bxb5 +299, loss 0.043 at 562/floor 800), SF19 d22 too, Lite mpv5 rank 5; no rule on Stockfish numbers can call it near-best.

different top move: SF16 d22 g6f5 +327 vs e1c1 +310 (17 cp), fresh SF19 Lite ranks e1c1 first; chess.com labels 17.Bf5 Excellent (not its top move), our dump has it top so the (fake, regain 4 for 2) bishop offer passes B-E4 margin 5.

different engine at the B-E2 boundary: 22...Rxh3 (exchange for bishop, rook left en prise to gxh3) is the top move for both engines, but SF19 Lite sees the alternative 22...Rg6 already winning (dump -608 for Black, ep 0.971 > 0.97 at the default 2500; fresh Lite second -596) while SF16 d22 has Rxh3 +527 vs Rg6 +439 for Black (ep 0.926, observer run +450: 0.930): on chess.com's engine numbers B-E2/B-E8 pass and our rules give Brilliant (SF19 cp ~1.3x SF16 above +200, observer scoperta 2).

different top move: 25.Bf8 (bishop offer, Kxf8? Rxh8+) is our Lite top (+614, second Bg5 +626 repeats into Bf8) but SF16 d22 ranks it 4th (+396 vs Bg5 +418, loss 0.011 at 2151; SF19 d22 2nd, 637 vs 641); chess.com labels it as a non-top move by its loss: Excellent.

engine scale: 30.Rxg6 (rook offer, sacrifice 3) is rank 2 in both engines (loss 0.007 Lite, 0.008 SF16) but the alternative 30.Qg2 is +906 for Lite (EP 0.971 at 1709: B-E2 > 0.97 and B-E8 >= +700, winning anyway) and +679 for SF16 d22 (EP 0.933): chess.com sees no decided position. SF19 cp ~1.3x SF16 above +400; moving the limits to SF19 scale costs 6-8 FP elsewhere.

different loss: 14.Nd5 (knight offer, sacrifice 3) is rank 2 in both engines but loses 0.034 for Lite (342 vs 275 at 890: over brilliantNonTopLoss 0.03, label Good) and 0.017 for SF16 d22 (236 vs 208; SF19 d22 0.030): within chess.com's non-top Brilliant tolerance only with its engine.

different top move: 54...Kc6 is not our Lite top (Kd6 -0.12 vs Kc6 +0.15 for White, label Excellent); SF16 d22 has Kb6 and Kc6 tied at +0.02, SF19 d22 ranks Kc6 first; chess.com had Kc6 as its top move and Great needs the top move.
different top move: 37.gxf4 is not our Lite top (exf4 +391 vs gxf4 +334, label Good); SF16 d22 ranks gxf4 first (+374 vs exf4 +358), SF19 d22 second (471 vs 474); Great needs the top move.

Different engine rank (shard 1): 20...Rd4 is the 2nd move for every engine: product Lite dump h5 -4.77 / Rd4 -3.79 (loss 0.041 > non-top 0.03), fresh Lite MultiPV h5 -336 / Rd4 -317, SF16 d22 h5 -337 / Rd4 -322 (rank 2), SF19 d22 rank 2. chess.com gives Brilliant to a sacrifice that is not its first move; as our first move it would be Brilliant (sacrifice 4). different engine (Great, CLAIMS cat. 1): 22.Nd4 is top for both, but SF19 Lite has Nd4 +0.01 vs c4 -1.89 (gap 0.127, cpGap 190: quiet branch fires at 1000) while SF16 d22 has Nd4 -65 vs c4 -141 (gap 0.051, cp 76: no branch fires); SF19 d22 gap 0.123. Our main eval is ~60 cp higher than SF16's.

different engine (Great): 11.Qxb8+ top for both; SF19 Lite second Qxc6 -1.32 (gap 0.077 at 1229, below every branch) while SF16 d22 has Qxb8+ -15 vs Qxc6 -372 (ep 0.489 -> 0.243: outcome class change, gap 0.246, cp 357; not free material, SEE < 0) = Great by our rules. Note: the observer's SF16 d22 run gave Qxc6 -142, the second line is unstable.

different engine (Great): 18.Nc3 top for both; SF19 Lite second Na3 -0.87 (ep 0.495 -> 0.409, still equal: gap 0.086) while SF16 d22 has Nc3 0 vs Na3 -128 (0.500 -> 0.368 losing: class change, gap 0.132, cp 128) = Great by our rules.
